tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a WhatsApp message to a person or group. For group chats use the JID.

recipient.description: The recipient - either a phone number with country code but no + or other symbols, or a JID (e.g., "123456789@s.whatsapp.net" or a group JID like "123456789@g.us")

tools.name: list_chats
tools.description: Get WhatsApp chats matching specified criteria.

query.description: Optional search term to filter chats by name or JID

limit.description: Maximum number of chats to return (default 20)

include_last_message.description: Whether to include the last message in each chat (default True)

sort_by.description: Field to sort results by, either "last_active" or "name" (default "last_active")

tools.name: search_contacts
tools.description: Search WhatsApp contacts by name or phone number.

query.description: Search term to match against contact names or phone numbers

tools.name: list_messages
tools.description: Get WhatsApp messages matching specified criteria with optional context.

after.description: Optional ISO-8601 formatted string to only return messages after this date

before.description: Optional ISO-8601 formatted string to only return messages before this date

sender_phone_number.description: Optional phone number to filter messages by sender

chat_jid.description: Optional chat JID to filter messages by chat

query.description: Optional search term to filter messages by content

limit.description: Maximum number of messages to return (default 20)

include_context.description: Whether to include messages before and after matches (default True)

context_before.description: Number of messages to include before each match (default 1)

context_after.description: Number of messages to include after each match (default 1)

tools.name: get_chat
tools.description: Get WhatsApp chat metadata by JID.

chat_jid.description: The JID of the chat to retrieve

include_last_message.description: Whether to include the last message (default True)

tools.name: get_direct_chat_by_contact
tools.description: Get WhatsApp chat metadata by sender phone number.

sender_phone_number.description: The phone number to search for

tools.name: get_contact_chats
tools.description: Get all WhatsApp chats involving the contact.

jid.description: The contact's JID to search for

limit.description: Maximum number of chats to return (default 20)

tools.name: get_last_interaction
tools.description: Get most recent WhatsApp message involving the contact.

jid.description: The JID of the contact to search for

tools.name: get_message_context
tools.description: Get context around a specific WhatsApp message.

message_id.description: The ID of the message to get context for

before.description: Number of messages to include before the target message (default 5)

after.description: Number of messages to include after the target message (default 5)

tools.name: send_file
tools.description: Send a file such as a picture, raw audio, video or document via WhatsApp to the specified recipient. For group messages use the JID.

recipient.description: The recipient - either a phone number with country code but no + or other symbols, or a JID (e.g., "123456789@s.whatsapp.net" or a group JID like "123456789@g.us")

media_path.description: The absolute path to the media file to send (image, video, document)

tools.name: send_audio_message
tools.description: Send any audio file as a WhatsApp audio message to the specified recipient. For group messages use the JID. If it errors due to ffmpeg not being installed, use send_file instead.

recipient.description: The recipient - either a phone number with country code but no + or other symbols, or a JID (e.g., "123456789@s.whatsapp.net" or a group JID like "123456789@g.us")

media_path.description: The absolute path to the audio file to send (will be converted to Opus .ogg if it's not a .ogg file)

tools.name: download_media
tools.description: Download media from a WhatsApp message and get the local file path.

message_id.description: The ID of the message containing the media

chat_jid.description: The JID of the chat containing the message

servers.description: Interacts with GitHub repositories, issues, pull requests, etc.

tools.name: get_issue
tools.description: Gets the contents of an issue within a repository.

tools.name: search_repositories
tools.description: Searches for GitHub repositories

tools.name: list_issues
tools.description: List and filter repository issues.

tools.name: get_pull_request
tools.description: Get details of a specific pull request.

tools.name: create_issue
tools.description: Create a new issue in a GitHub repository.

assignees.description: Usernames to assign to this issue (string[], optional)

labels.description: Labels to apply to this issue (string[], optional)

tools.name: get_pull_request_files
tools.description: Get files for a specific pull request.

tools.name: get_pull_request_status
tools.description: Get status for a specific pull request.

tools.name: update_pull_request_branch
tools.description: Update a pull request branch.

tools.name: get_pull_request_comments
tools.description: Get comments for a specific pull request.

tools.name: get_pull_request_reviews
tools.description: Get reviews for a specific pull request.

tools.name: create_pull_request_review
tools.description: Create a review for a specific pull request.

event.description: The event to perform on the pull request review. Can be one of: APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES, COMMENT (string, optional)

tools.name: create_pull_request
tools.description: Create a pull request.

title.description: The title of the pull request (string, required)

head.description: The name of the branch where your changes are implemented (string, required)

base.description: The name of the branch you want the changes pulled into (string, required)

body.description: The contents of the pull request (string, optional)

tools.name: update_pull_request
tools.description: Update a pull request.

title.description: The title of the pull request (string, optional)

body.description: The contents of the pull request (string, optional)

state.description: State of the pull request. Can be open or closed (string, optional)

tools.name: create_or_update_file
tools.description: Create or update a file in a repository.

path.description: The path to the file (string, required)

content.description: File content, which must be base64 encoded (string, required)

branch.description: The name of the branch you want to make the commit on (string, optional)

tools.name: push_files
tools.description: Push multiple files to a repository.

branch.description: The name of the branch you want to make the commit on (string, required)

files.description: List of files to push (string[], required)

tools.name: create_repository
tools.description: Create a new repository.

name.description: The name of the repository (string, required)

description.description: A short description of the repository (string, optional)

private.description: Whether the repository should be private (boolean, optional)

tools.name: get_file_contents
tools.description: Get the contents of a file in a repository.

path.description: The path to the file (string, required)

ref.description: The name of the commit/branch/tag. Defaults to the repository’s default branch (string, optional)

tools.name: fork_repository
tools.description: Fork a repository.

tools.name: create_branch
tools.description: Create a branch in a repository.

branch.description: The name of the new branch (string, required)

sha.description: The commit SHA to create the branch from (string, required)

tools.name: list_commits
tools.description: List commits in a repository.

sha.description: SHA or branch to start listing commits from (string, optional)

path.description: Only commits containing this file path will be returned (string, optional)

author.description: GitHub login or email address by which to filter by commit author (string, optional)

since.description: Only show commits after this date. This is a timestamp in ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ (string, optional)

until.description: Only show commits before this date. This is a timestamp in ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ (string, optional)

tools.name: search_code
tools.description: Search code in a repository.

q.description: The search terms. This can be any combination of the supported code search qualifiers (string, required)

sort.description: Sort matches by size or path (string, optional)

order.description: Determines whether the first search result returned is the highest number of matches (string, optional)

page.description: Page number of the results to fetch (number, optional)

tools.name: search_users
tools.description: Search users on GitHub.

sort.description: Sort matches by followers, repositories, or joined (string, optional)

order.description: Determines whether the first search result returned is the highest number of matches (string, optional)

page.description: Page number of the results to fetch (number, optional)

tools.name: get_code_scanning_alert
tools.description: Get a code scanning alert.

alert_number.description: The number that identifies an alert. (number, required)

tools.name: list_code_scanning_alerts
tools.description: List code scanning alerts.

state.description: The state of the code scanning alerts to list. Can be: open, dismissed, or all (string, optional)

severity.description: The severity of the code scanning alerts to list. Can be: critical, high, medium, low, or warning (string, optional)

sort.description: The property to sort the results by. Can be: created_at or state (string, optional)

direction.description: The direction to sort the results by. Can be: asc or desc (string, optional)

page.description: Page number of the results to fetch (number, optional)

servers.description: Manages Gmail and Google Calendar interactions.

tools.name: query_gmail_emails
tools.description: Query Gmail emails based on an optional search query. Returns emails in reverse chronological order (newest first). Returns metadata such as subject and also a short summary of the content.

query.description:
Gmail search query (optional). Examples:
- a $string: Search email body, subject, and sender information for $string
- 'is:unread' for unread emails
- 'from:example@gmail.com' for emails from a specific sender
- 'newer_than:2d' for emails from last 2 days
- 'has:attachment' for emails with attachments
If not provided, returns recent emails without filtering.

max_results.description: Maximum number of emails to retrieve (1-500)

tools.name: get_calendar_events
tools.description: Retrieves calendar events from the user's Google Calendar within a specified time range.

__calendar_id__.description:
Optional ID of the specific agenda for which you are executing this action.
                          If not provided, the default calendar is being used. 
                          If not known, the specific calendar id can be retrieved with the list_calendars tool

time_min.description: Start time in RFC3339 format (e.g. 2024-12-01T00:00:00Z). Defaults to current time if not specified.

time_max.description: End time in RFC3339 format (e.g. 2024-12-31T23:59:59Z). Optional.

max_results.description: Maximum number of events to return (1-2500)

tools.name: list_calendars
tools.description:
Lists all calendars accessible by the user. 
            Call it before any other tool whenever the user specifies a particular agenda (Family, Holidays, etc.).

tools.name: create_calendar_event
tools.description: Creates a new event in a specified Google Calendar of the specified user.

__calendar_id__.description:
Optional ID of the specific agenda for which you are executing this action.
                          If not provided, the default calendar is being used. 
                          If not known, the specific calendar id can be retrieved with the list_calendars tool

description.description: Description or notes for the event (optional)

send_notifications.description: Whether to send notifications to attendees

timezone.description: Timezone for the event (e.g. 'America/New_York'). Defaults to UTC if not specified.

tools.name: delete_calendar_event
tools.description: Deletes an event from the user's Google Calendar by its event ID.

__calendar_id__.description:
Optional ID of the specific agenda for which you are executing this action.
                          If not provided, the default calendar is being used. 
                          If not known, the specific calendar id can be retrieved with the list_calendars tool

event_id.description: The ID of the calendar event to delete

send_notifications.description: Whether to send cancellation notifications to attendees

tools.name: get_gmail_email
tools.description: Retrieves a complete Gmail email message by its ID, including the full message body and attachment IDs.

email_id.description: The ID of the Gmail message to retrieve

tools.name: bulk_get_gmail_emails
tools.description: Retrieves multiple Gmail email messages by their IDs in a single request, including the full message bodies and attachment IDs.

email_ids.description: List of Gmail message IDs to retrieve

tools.name: create_gmail_draft
tools.description:
Creates a draft email message from scratch in Gmail with specified recipient, subject, body, and optional CC recipients.
            
            Do NOT use this tool when you want to draft or send a REPLY to an existing message. This tool does NOT include any previous message content. Use the reply_gmail_email tool
            with send=False instead.

cc.description: Optional list of email addresses to CC

tools.name: delete_gmail_draft
tools.description: Deletes a Gmail draft message by its ID. This action cannot be undone.

draft_id.description: The ID of the draft to delete

tools.name: reply_gmail_email
tools.description:
Creates a reply to an existing Gmail email message and either sends it or saves as draft.

            Use this tool if you want to draft a reply. Use the 'cc' argument if you want to perform a "reply all".

original_message_id.description: The ID of the Gmail message to reply to

reply_body.description: The body content of your reply message

send.description: If true, sends the reply immediately. If false, saves as draft.

cc.description: Optional list of email addresses to CC on the reply

tools.name: get_gmail_attachment
tools.description: Retrieves a Gmail attachment by its ID.

message_id.description: The ID of the Gmail message containing the attachment

attachment_id.description: The ID of the attachment to retrieve

mime_type.description: The MIME type of the attachment

save_to_disk.description: The fullpath to save the attachment to disk. If not provided, the attachment is returned as a resource.

tools.name: bulk_save_gmail_attachments
tools.description: Saves multiple Gmail attachments to disk by their message IDs and attachment IDs in a single request.

message_id.description: ID of the Gmail message containing the attachment

part_id.description: ID of the part containing the attachment

save_path.description: Path where the attachment should be saved

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search DuckDuckGo and return formatted results.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 10)

tools.name: fetch_content
tools.description: Fetch and parse content from a webpage URL.

url.description: The webpage URL to fetch content from
